name: BTS7004-1EPP
title: PROFET +2 12V single-channel 4.4 mΩ smart high-side power switch
summary: A one-channel 12 V smart high-side switch with a 4.4 mΩ (typ, 25 °C) N-channel output, rated for 15 A nominal at 85 °C ambient. It protects itself against overtemperature, overload, overvoltage and reverse battery, and reports load current, open load and shorts on one IS pin as a proportional or fixed current. AEC-Q100 Grade 1, PG-TSDSO-14 with exposed pad.
key_figures: 4.1 V to 28 V (3.1 V while cranking)

circuits.title: Application diagram
circuits.description: One microcontroller runs the switch. Two GPIOs reach IN and DEN through 4.7 kΩ resistors (RIN, RDEN), which also keep the output off if the module ground is lost. The IS current develops a voltage across RSENSE (1.2 kΩ) and reaches the ADC through RIS_PROT and RADC (4.7 kΩ each), with the 7 V Zener DZ1 between them and CSENSE (220 pF) at the ADC pin forming a filter. The battery arrives over the harness at VS, with CVS (100 nF) to module ground, the optional CVSGND (47 nF) to the device GND pin, the 33 V TVS DZ2 and the buffer CVS2. The device GND pin returns to module ground through RGND (47 Ω). On the output, RPD (47 kΩ) and COUT0 (10 nF) go to ground, and the optional PNP T1 with ROL (1.5 kΩ) pulls the output up for open load diagnosis in OFF. Logic and power grounds meet at one star point that is tied to chassis ground, where the load returns.

operation.text: A single-channel 12 V high-side switch of the PROFET +2 family: its output an N-channel vertical power MOSFET driven by a charge pump, 4.4 mΩ typical, with load current sense, open-load detection in ON and OFF, short-circuit detection to ground and battery, absolute and dynamic overtemperature limits, overcurrent trip with an intelligent latch, undervoltage shutdown, ReverseON in reverse polarity and InverseON. Qualified to AEC-Q100 Grade 1. Intended for 15 A resistive, inductive and capacitive loads such as glow plugs, heaters, DC motors and power distribution, in place of relays, fuses and discrete circuits.

IN turns the channel on when high; DEN enables diagnosis when high and a high-to-low edge on it can clear the protection latch. Both inputs share one structure, a clamp to GND, and work from 3.3 V and 5 V microcontrollers. The voltage that guarantees high is always above the one that guarantees low (threshold VDI(TH), hysteresis VDI(HYS)). An unused input goes to the GND pin or module ground through 4.7 kΩ. With DEN low the IS pin is high impedance; DEN does not disable the protection.

Above VS(OP) the part is in OFF, ON, OFF_Diag, ON_Diag or Fault mode, chosen by IN, DEN and the internal latch. In OFF the supply draw is IVS(OFF) and neither protection nor diagnosis runs. In ON (IN high, DEN low) overcurrent and overtemperature protection run with no diagnosis; consumption is measured at the GND pin, IGND(ON_D) + IIS(OFF), since VS carries the load current. OFF_Diag (IN low, DEN high) puts IIS(FAULT) or IIS(OLOFF) on IS depending on the load, raising consumption. ON_Diag has the sense output on, consumption IGND(ON_D). Fault mode follows any protective switch-off; IIS(FAULT) appears on IS while DEN is high.

Below VS(OP) the output stage and diagnosis are held off. When the channel is on and VS sinks under VS(UV) the channel turns off; once VS climbs back over VS(OP) it turns on again after tDELAY(UV), which guards against a short circuit that pulls the supply down (AEC-Q100-012). From OFF mode with IN high the channel turns on as soon as VS exceeds VS(OP), with no delay. If an overload trip drags VS into the VS(EXT,CVG) range and the retry count differs from the intelligent latch behaviour, CVSGND is required.
RDS(ON) rises with junction temperature; its variation factor is normalised so that 2 equals the 150 °C maximum.
Turn-on and turn-off delays, times and slew rates are taken between 10 %, 30 %, 70 % and 90 % of VS on VOUT. The switching energies EON and EOFF scale with load resistance and with tON and tOFF.
At turn-off an inductive load drives VOUT below ground. A clamp holds VDS at VDS(CLAMP) in every operating mode, and the switch absorbs the stored energy; EAS and EAR bound it.
With DEN high, if falling load current brings VDS down to VDS(SLC), the gate is partly discharged so VDS stays at VDS(SLC) even at very small currents. This improves kILIS accuracy at low load.

When VOUT exceeds VS, current IINV flows back through the output transistor. Off, it passes the body diode with high loss; on, the drop follows RDS(INV), close to normal operation. The channel keeps its state while |IL| < |IL(INV)|, and InverseON lets it be switched on during inverse current within that limit. Overtemperature and overload protection do not act while inverse current flows.

Paired with a low-side switch in a bridge, the slope the low-side switch forces on OUT must stay under |dVOUT / dt| (10 V/µs max). A faster slope can turn the output stage on in linear mode during commutation, overheating the DMOS with unprotected cross-conduction current.

Two limits watch the channel: an absolute one, TJ(ABS), and a dynamic one, TJ(DYN), referred to a reference temperature TJ(REF). Crossing either turns the channel off until the reactivation condition is met, after which the intelligent latch decides when it may turn on again.

Overload or short circuit to ground trips the channel at IL(OVL). The threshold depends on VDS: IL(OVL0) below 13 V, IL(OVL1) above 22 V, with a linear fall between 15 V and 20 V on the typical curve. It is highest when cold, for inrush at low ambient, and its typical value stays near constant up to about +75 °C before falling. Whenever VS reaches VS(JS) (load dump, jump start) the threshold drops to IL(OVL_JS); the switch-over lies between VS(JS),min and VS(JS),max.

operation.topic: Fault latch and IS fault signal
operation.text: A protective trip turns the channel off and sets the internal latch to 1; with diagnosis on, IS delivers IIS(FAULT). The latch clears in two ways. Holding IN low for longer than tDELAY(LR) clears it, and a high on IN during that time restarts the timer. A DEN pulse (rise then fall) longer than tDEN(LR) while IN is low clears it at once. Restart is allowed only when the reactivation conditions hold: for overload, IL below 50 mA and TJ inside both thermal limits.

With battery reversed, ReverseON turns the output stage on (RDS(REV)) to cut its dissipation; the logic ESD diodes add to the loss. The load must limit the reverse current through the output, and series resistors must limit the input currents. ReverseON needs current flowing out of the GND pin, so a resistive path from module ground to the GND pin must exist.
For supplies from VS(EXT,UP) up to VBAT(LD), IN still controls the output. Besides the output clamp, a clamp from VS to GND (VS(CLAMP)) protects the logic and the channel.

operation.topic: Loss of battery, load or ground
operation.text: With purely resistive load and harness, losing battery or load does no harm. With inductance the stored energy must go somewhere: the family handles harness inductance up to 10 µH at IL(NOM); beyond that an external suppressor such as DZ2 gives the current a path. On loss of device ground, series resistors on the digital inputs make sure the channel turns off; an input pulled to ground offers a parasitic ground path that can keep the device running.

IS carries the diagnosis current; with DEN low it is high impedance. When current sense is used, RSENSE goes from IS to module ground and must exceed 820 Ω (400 Ω with central reverse battery protection on the feed) to limit losses; 1.2 kΩ is typical. IS is tied internally to VS, so it should not share a line with sense outputs of devices on another battery feed.

IS gives IL / kILIS when the stage is on with VDS < VDS(OLOFF), diagnosis is enabled and no uncleared fault exists. IIS rises linearly with IL up to IIS(SAT); near zero load the current is IIS(EN). An RC filter of at least 1 µs between IS and the ADC reduces ripple. kILIS limits cover temperature, supply and process; calibration at one current IL(CAL) at TA(CAL) = 25 °C at end of line narrows them to ΔkILIS across IL(CAL)_L to IL(CAL)_H, drift over temperature and current included.
Once the latch is 1 and not cleared, IIS(FAULT) is delivered every time DEN goes high, in ON and in OFF, regardless of VDS or VOUT.

In OFF with DEN high, VDS is compared with VDS(OLOFF). A connected load and no short to battery give VDS near VS, above the threshold. With VDS at or below VDS(OLOFF), IS delivers IIS(OLOFF), whose range does not overlap IIS(FAULT). An output pull-down resistor plus a pull-up current that can be switched in make open load and short to battery detectable. Allow tIS(OLOFF)_D after IN falls before reading IS.

The sense signal settles within tsIS(ON) after DEN rises, within tsIS(LC) after a load step, and is gone within tsIS(OFF) after DEN falls. A valid signal needs a settled load current, so after switch-on tsIS(DIAG) is at most 3 × (tON_max + tsIS(ON)_max).

Thermal figures come from simulation on a 1.5 mm FR4 board: 1s0p with 70 µm copper (traces and cooling area modelled, 5 % metal elsewhere) at footprint, 300 mm² and 600 mm² cooling area, and 2s2p with 70 µm outer and 35 µm inner layers at 90 % metal, with thermal vias under the exposed pad.
All six OUT pins are joined inside and must all be joined on the board, with traces sized for the highest current that can flow. The exposed pad is VS.
PG-TSDSO-14 with exposed pad, marking 7004-1P. RoHS-compliant green product with Pb-free finish, suitable for Pb-free soldering to IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020.
